observations: A tall black vertical form on the left, segmented at a joint midway down, stands apart from the main mass and carries thin white lines tracing its interior edges.
The upper mass is dense black with sharp spiked protrusions at the top and a grid of white lines inside a roughly oval cavity, giving the solid area a hollow, latticed quality.
Loose trailing lines descend from the right side of the upper mass and gather into a crouched lower form, while a thin horizontal baseline and a small signed mark sit in the lower-left corner.
reading: Two forms share weight without quite touching: the isolated limb on the left and the compressed bulk above suggest strain or suspension rather than rest. White lines scratched into the black mass give the dense areas a hollow feeling, as if the solid shapes are shells. The trailing lines on the right pull the eye downward against the upward spikes.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between nnotb #147—color-saturated with a framed skull form on deep red—and nnotb #149, dense with layered spirals and warm hues. #148 is the starkest of the three, working entirely in black and white.

connections.reason: Both works use black fill with white lines across interior surfaces to suggest depth inside solid forms, and both place a dense upper mass above a more open lower zone.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the white lines inside the black mass begin and end, and does that boundary change how you read the relationship between the two separated forms?
ambiguities: The lower crouched form is ambiguous—its outlines suggest a figure but the lines do not resolve into clearly identifiable anatomy.
nnotb #149 shares title-order and recorded-creation adjacency but its dense color spirals offer no strong formal echo with #148's monochrome structure, so it was not selected as a connection.
